Several months later, in an interview to a "Ratne Novine" journalist on the 24th of November, 1991, he speaks in favour of a population in change, suggesting that the Serbs from Zagreb should go to Zupanja and that the Croats from Zupanja should go to settle in Zagreb, because, in his view, Croats and Serbs cannot cohabit, live together, within one and the same state. I insist, he said, that the Serbs and Croats could not live together within one and the same state. Exhibit P1186. The following year, in 1992, he gave an interview to a Radio Novi Sad reporter on the 6th of January, 1992, and he called for a population exchange between Serbs and Croats which should be done as soon as possible in his view. Exhibit P1190. On the 5th of April, 1992, he gave an interview to a "Politika" journalist and spoke in favour of a population exchange between Serbs and Croats. Exhibit P1298. In an interview to a journalist of the "Unity" Serb daily, I spoke about it already, but this was on the 21st of April, 1992, he urged the 500.000 Albanian migrants to go back to Albania. Exhibit P1197. In questions during a press conference held by the SRS on the 28th of May, 1992, the accused stated that the disloyal Croats should be ousted from Croatia, deported from Croatia and that the Serb refugees should actually take their place in the dwellings that they should have left. Exhibit P1199. On the 12th of June, 1992, he stated to TV "Politika" that there was going to be an exchange population between Serbs and Croats. Exhibit P1201. In an interview to a "Globus" journalist on the 7th of August, 1992, he explained that when the SRS was in power, he -- it would carry out a population exchange between Serbs and Croats. Exhibit P1203. In a debate organised by the "Tanjug" news agency on the 7th of December, 1992, he called for the deportation of the 360.000 Albanian migrants and their offsprings who had entered Kosovo-Metohija, or, more widely, Yugoslavia, since the 6th of April 1941. Exhibit P1208. Let's move to 1993. Sorry for speeding up. My apologies to the interpreters, but since they are excellent, they're able to keep pace with me. In a radio interview to Radio Banja Luka, 20th of March, 1993, he said that the SRS had worked to accommodate Serb refugees in abandoned flats. He said that there should be a campaign for a population exchange between Serbs, Muslims and Croats who no longer can, according to him, live together in the same territory. Exhibit P1215. In a radio interview to Radio Belgrade on the 22nd of March, 1993, he explained that Dobrica Cosic, president of the FRI, called for a population exchange between Serbs and Croats and that the SRS was fully committed to make it happen. Exhibit P1216. In an interview, the source of which is not specified but it is mentioned in one of his books, the accused -- this is Exhibit P1218. So on the 7th of May, 1993, he said that there was a spontaneous population exchange in Zvornik whereby the Serbs took the place of the former Muslim inhabitants. On the 4th of November, 1993, speaking to radio "Ponos," he called for a population exchange. Exhibit P1231. On the 6th of December, 1993, speaking to a "Tanjug" journalist, he admitted that he had held propaganda speeches for the population to leave Serbia. Document of P574 of 20th of September from the Republic of Serbia noted that during the 2002 census, there were 56.546 civilians living in the autonomous province of Vojvoda; whilst, according to the 1991 census, there were 74.808 of them. And, therefore, there were 18.262 less civilians. That is a reduction of 24.41 per cent, and this document shows that this reduction results from the policy of persecution against a civilian population which can amount to a war crime. This document might be such as to support the Prosecution's allegation as to a policy of persecution that led to the transfer and deportation of non-Serbs. In paragraph 11 of their pre-trial brief, the Prosecution said that the speeches by the accused became more and more virulent towards the Serbian Croats. Exhibits P35, P892, P43. It said that the accused said that once there would have been thousands of federal officials deported, thousands of dwellings would have become available in Belgrade. This refers explicitly to the departure of officials from the federal structures of the former Yugoslavia. There's also an allusion to the population exchange speaking about Serbs deported from Zagreb and these are classic retaliation measures in international law. Basically saying: We're not going to kill you, of course, but we're going to make sure that you get on board trucks and on trains wound bound for Zagreb. P892. In document P43 admitted that he would depart Croats for several reasons: Because they're not faithful to Serbia, they destabilise the domestic situation, they turned out to be direct Ustasha collaborationists, and, finally, because they must be the target of retaliation measures after the deportation of 160.000 Serbs by Tudjman. As to the issue which is at the very core of the problem. This was the question you were criticised because you said that all the Croats had to be deported from Serbia, and therefore -- it's not in the SRS tradition to -- to say so. And so that question is put but he doesn't really answer it. He just says that the SRS will tackle the problem at the root of the cause and the person asking the questions realise that they don't get the answer they wish for, and he says: "Now are you going to withdraw what you said about the Croats?" And then the accused said" "Never, ever." Is such an answer directly connected to deportation or to the arguments by Croats who deported Serbs? In this respect, I do not have an absolute certainty. Do I have a doubt. When Ms. Tabeau testified in support of her report on the immigrations of Croats and other non-Serb population from the Hrtkovci village in 1992, there was a list of Croats who left that place in 1992, P565, the destination being Croatia or unknown destination I mentioned that last time. The migration of the Hrtkovci population in her view was confirmed by information gathered by the Office for Displaced Persons and Refugees established by the Croatian authorities. The latter was to count the arrivals and assess their situation to see that they were entitled to the status of displaced persons and possibly to be given a registration number each. This is transcript page 10842. Witness VS-061 said that baptism certificates were given to Croats leaving Hrtkovci so that they could move and cross over to Croatia. Transcript pages 9930, 9931, 9937, 9954. A reasonable trier of fact could therefore find that among the 722 names listed, there are, in fact, 233 of them with unknown destination and they have to be taken out of that list. Finally, a reasonable trier of fact whom I decide to find the accused guilty for the crime of deportation and forcible transfer in Hrtkovci between 1992 and 1993 can only find him guilty on the basis of the deportation or transfer of 489 individuals in Annex 11 of the indictment. Based on the evidence, a reasonable trier of fact might find that the accused has committed crimes of deportation and forcible transfer as defined in Counts 10 and 11 of the indictment. I'm just about done as far as the D chapter. Now let's move to aiding and abetting. Regarding the mode of responsibility connected to aiding and abetting, the Prosecution in paragraphs 149, 150, 151, 152 and 153 of its preliminary -- of its preliminary brief uses a large amount of jurisprudence in it's foot notes 507 to 513, Aleksovski, Krnojelac, Kunarac, Blaskic, Furundzija, Tadic, Celebici, and Vasiljevic, to state that aiding and abetting means providing help, encouragement, or moral support to the person committing the crime. The case law says that the act of an accused must have an important or significant effect on the perpetration of the crime. Aiding and abetting can be done before, during or after the crime. The presence of the accused may constitute a form of aiding and abetting if it had the effect of the physical perpetrator. The mens rea must have two aspects. First, the accused must be aware that the commission of the crime is foreseeable, and the accused must know that his acts will contribute to the commission of the crime by the physical perpetrator. According to the Prosecution in paragraph 153, the mens rea is proved by his own statements, P644, the inflammatory nature of his speeches, his repeated visits to the battle field, and the fact that he relentlessly sent volunteers on the front. Witness VS-017 by his orders sent to the volunteers and other Serbian forces, Witnesses VS-007, VS-026, and VS-027, and the omission of taking any sanctions against volunteers whenever crimes were committed. VS-007, VS-026 and VS-034. Therefore, it seems that adding and abetting results from the words uttered by the accused but the fact that he was present before on the battle-field before the combat and sending volunteers. In the indictment, there are three regions Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia and Serbia. Now you have to relocate the crimes in these regions, put them back in perspective in these two regions with two main dates in mind: The declaration of independence of Croatia and the declaration of independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. These two dates are extremely important because their effect was the JNA was withdrawn and was replaced by local forces or armed groups which came from regional entities so the question now is whether Serbia actually controlled the troops on the ground. The control by Serbia of -- on Serbian forces, as the case law of the Tribunal is concerned, must be a global control with the control of military operations and not just a financial support. In paragraph 137, of the Tadic appeals judgement this is what the -- what was said: "The control required by international law may be deemed to exist when a state has a role in organising, co-ordinating or planning the military actions of the military group. In addition, to financing training and equipping or providing operational support to that group." We still have ten minutes before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even more, actually, because we resumed at 4.25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Lattanzi says we still have 20 minutes and I thank her for that. Regarding overall control, the International Court of Justice, in the appeals judgement application of the convention for the prevention and repression of crimes of genocide Bosnia-Herzegovina versus Serbia and Montenegro, a world-known appeals judgement dated February 26th, 2007, concluded that Serbia did not have an overall control over the soldiers of the VRS because the VRS was not a de jure organ of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in the sense that did not have under its domestic law the status of organ of this one. In paragraph 392, and following of this appeals judgement, this is what is said by the International Court of Justice. I will read slowly because this is important: "According to the Court's jurisprudence, persons, groups of persons or entities may, for purpose of the international responsibility, be acquainted with state organs even if that status does not follow from internal law provided that, in fact, the persons, groups or entities act in complete dependence," I quote, "complete dependence on the state of which they are ultimately merely the instrument." Next paragraph, it's also absolutely essential: "At the relevant time, July 1995, neither the Republika Srpska nor the VRS could be regarded as mere instruments through which the FRY was acting and is lacking any real autonomy, while the political, military and logistical relation between the federal authorities of Belgrade and the authorities in Pale between the Yugoslav army and the VRS had been strong and close in the previous years and these ties undoubtedly remained powerful. They were at least at the relevant time not such that the Bosnian Serbs political and military organisation should be equated with organs of the FRY." The Judges of the ICJ in order to reach this conclusion, this essential conclusion, were provided with the judgements and the documents of this Tribunal. Therefore, this is the question now. If Serbia does not have overall control over the soldiers of VRS, how could a political opponent such as Mr. Seselj have such a control? Therefore, the accused is charged for having aided and abetted all crimes on Counts 1 to 14 by contributing individually and in full awareness. But this mode of liability is extremely broad and must be examined and reviewed for each count. It is important to establish at least that between the crimes committed and the accused, there's some kind of nexus out of his behaviour and his speeches. Firstly, there is no evidence as far as Count 4, murder; Counts 8 and 9, torture and cruel treatment; and Counts 12 to 14, wanton discretion and plunder. Through his behaviour and his speech, the Prosecution does not establish beyond any reasonable doubt that he aided and abetted those who actually committed the murders, tortures, plunders or looting. Contrary to this in Exhibit P644, and I think Mr. Marcussen should read it, it is a key Prosecution evidence. Well, it shows that all these counts are condemned by the accused himself in March 1995. This is what he said: "There were incidents and we were extremely strict on the front line. We immediately dismissed these people. "These policemen and Arkan's men started to ransack the town. It was a large -cale plunder. "When half of the operation was over, in Zvornik they started to plunder. They even looted the Serbs. "It's Commander Arkan who organised this cleansing of Muslims." And he is using the word "cleansing": "These Muslims were killed and the regime does not want to disclose anything about this. Those who killed them came from Belgrade." Regarding Bijeljina, he says: "Arkan was under the control of Karadzic or under the control of the Serbian Army, and later under the orders of Blagojevic. He was prevented from playing any role because he had committed the plunder in Bijeljina. He had 15 men over there. "The situation there was difficult because there were many crimes." And then I quote one last sentence which is also essential. This is what he says: "Ethnic cleansing was --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to intervene once again, even though I don't do it gladly. Could you please be more precise when it comes to Arkan. I think that the interpretation into Serbian and interpretation into English were the opposite of what I said. I said that Arkan could not be under the control, either Karadzic or the Serbian Army or Blagojevic, and it was interpreted as though Arkan was under their control. I didn't hear the French original very well, but I would like you to repeat that sentence, if possible, and then we should check the original. Arkan was beyond anyone's control. This is what I meant. This is what I said, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will look at document P644 in detail. Unless there was a mistake in translation, this is what was said. But in French it's alleged you would have said, "Arkan was -- was under the control of Karadzic or under the control of the Serbian Army and later under the orders of Blagojevic -- Blagovic." There might be a mistaken but this is on the paper I'm reading. The last sentence which is the most important -- this is what you allegedly would have said, unless there was an error, of course, and giving the reference of the document, it's a video 02.45.59. This is what you would have said: "Ethnic cleansing was not organised, but of course there's -- there have been, here and there, certain events where some form of ethnic cleansing occurred." This is what you said. However, Counts 1, 10, and 11 can fall under the liability of the accused regarding aiding and abetting through the inflammatory nature of his speech. Consequently, the accused should be acquitted of aiding and abetting for Counts 4, 8, 9, 12 to 14, and could - I'm now saying could and not should -- could be found guilty as evidence stands now for Counts 1, 10, and 11, subject to no evidence to the contrary being adduced by the accused during the presentation of his case. I have one last chapter on the counts, counts 1, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, and 14, and I intended to detail them. I wanted to run through them, one after the other. Count 1, for example, persecution, I would say, non-Serb civilian population from territories of the SAO SBS -- SBWS, et cetera, et cetera. I based myself on the preliminary brief to make a list of all this, but I believe that this is not fundamental. But what is absolutely fundamental, and I will ask Mr. Usher to help us, could he please place on the ELMO my conclusion to know exactly where I would enter an acquittal and where, if possibly given the evidence adduced, and so on, as a reasonable Judge and beyond any other -- any -- beyond any reasonable doubt I could find you guilty according to -- under Rule 98 bis. This is Appendix 13. I've given all the elements adduced so far. You would be acquitted regarding planning on Counts 1, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14. Regarding instigating, acquitted on Counts 4 8, 9, 12, 13 and 14. Regarding ordering, acquitted on Counts 1, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14. Regarding committing, I would enter a judgement of acquittal. Since I did not retain the JCE, I would acquit you for 1, 2, and 3 of the JCE, and for aiding and abetting, you would be acquitted on Counts 4, 8, 9, 12, 13 and 14. I shall now show you Annex 14, which is a summary table of what I admit based on the evidence provided by the Prosecution. Notwithstanding what you will say during your defence case, based on all the evidence adduced, I would like to say as far as instigation is concerned, I could enter a conviction of guilty for persecution Counts 10 and 11, deportation and forcible transfer. For the material commission, I could enter a conviction of guilt under Counts 1, 10, and 11. For deportation and forced -- forcible transfer, and as regards aiding and abetting, I could also admit Counts 1, persecution; 10 and 11, deportation, and forcible transfer. I must -- or I lastly have the duty to say, as you can see on the screen, that, for the time being, I have admitted the following forms: Instigation -- these are forms of responsibility: Instigating, aiding and abetting, committing. Based on the evidence adduced but at the time of the judgement, it will be important to admit only one form of responsibility, for either the accused committed, either he instigated, or he aided and abetted. In my view, it can only be an either/or situation. You can't be an instigator, accomplice and perpetrator all at once. This concludes my opinion. All of this is very complicated in technical terms. I fully agree with the Trial Chamber as regards persecution through instigation instigating committing and aiding and abetting. However, I totally disagree about the fact and I also agree on the count relating to forcible transfer and deportation. I fully agree with the majority of the Chamber as regards Counts 1, 10, and 11, and the Chamber in its majority held that all the other counts needed to be addressed. There is a diverging view on this matter. Like my colleagues, I'm in favour of the continuance of the trial and I dismiss your motion for grounds that differ from the grounds put forward by my colleagues. We now have a make a break, which is a 60-minute break. These are for technical reasons. Thirty minutes, 30 minutes. I'm sorry. We shall resume in 30 minutes' time, and in 30 minutes' time, I will tell Mr. Seselj how we proceed further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The court is back in session. I have three corrections of a technical nature to make since all this was very quick. I would like on page 43, line 23, a correction to be made. Instead of a 1033, it was Witness VS-1133. Second correction of a technical nature: On page 44, line 16, instead of VS-1136, it should read 1036. Third correction: Judge Harhoff drew my attention on a quotation I made of a footnote, which was 429. I had said that during that period a unit of the Special of Sremska Mitrovica was seconded to Hrtkovci prevented the Serbs -- or the non-Serb population from being attacked. This established the fact that there could be no collusion, because the authorities had sent police forces. Judge Harhoff remarked that it was also stated in this paragraph, and I quoted, so that we have it in full, that this unit did not protect the village and sometimes even helped the SCP leaders to drive out some of the Croats. I did not deliberately read out the second part, because what I was interested in was to establish that the authorities had sent a unit and that if this unit had formed a pact with the people living in that locality, I was interested in the fact that the authorities had sent some men there, and what I had in mind was what is happening in Libya today, or in Syria, for instance, where units are sent there by the authorities, and once they're on the ground they form a pact with the people on the ground. What is important is to know that the authorities did send a unit there. That is what I wanted to highlight, the fact that they did collude or that they did the contrary of what the assignment was all about. That is a different issue. That said, Mr. Seselj, the Chamber has decided to proceed with the trial, and pursuant to Rule 65 ter (G), I shall read to you what you need to do. The ball is now in your camp. After the presentation the Prosecution and the Defence case, the Pre-Trial Judge ordered the Defence to file the following. Therefore, you need to give us a list of witnesses that you intend to call. You must specify the name or pseudonym of each witness, a summary of the facts on which each witness will testify, the points in the indictment on which each witness will testify, the total number of witnesses and number of witnesses who will testify on each count. If the witness testifies pursuant to 92 bis or 92 quater, this could also be part of Rule 92 ter. The statement of -- given by the testimony and the length of -- the length of the testimony and list of exhibits is important. The Trial Chamber met on a number of occasions and decided, as of today onwards, to grant you six weeks, which means that we should have this list by the 17th of June. As you know, the Prosecutor will certainly make observations following that in the event that you do give this list, and the Trial Chamber will hand down a decision, and bear in mind the various deadlines in the event that this happens this way. It is quite possible that we can start hearing your witnesses after the recess. The 15th of June decision rendered by the Chamber, we will then be in July already, and that will probably be after the summer recess only at the bare minimum. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I cannot file any of the lists you mentioned within that deadline or any of the requested information unless certain preconditions are met based on my fundamental rights. First of all, you have to regulate the status of Zoran Krasic as my legal advisor. From the first day of my stay here, the Trial Chamber denied certain status rights to Zoran Rankic, because you decided that he was not allowed to be present in the courtroom when confidential evidence is being heard. If my legal advisor Zoran Krasic does not have the equal status with all other legal advisors, I will not be presenting my Defence case. Secondly, the Registry has started disciplinary proceedings against my legal advisor Boris Aleksic. He sent a request to the Association of Defence Counsel here in The Hague, even though he's not a Defence counsel nor a member of that counsel association, but a commission has been established headed by Edina Residovic, a lawyer, a well-known lawyer from the proceedings against Izetbegovic who also appeared in Sarajevo back in 1984 at my initial appearance in a court in Sarajevo. She represented the Prosecution at the time, and now she was appointed as president of this disciplinary commission. Unless there harassment of Boris Aleksic, my legal advisor, does not stop immediately, I will not be presenting my Defence case. Next, the financing of my Defence has not been resolved yet. You made a decision concerning the Registry, decision prior to that. I will not be appealing it, because in your decision you ruled that my legal advisors are to be remunerated at the rate of 50 -- at the rate of 50 per cent for the accused. However, you have not ruled anything concerning the retroactive payments for the past eight years. These people worked hard with me. They wrote thousands and thousands of pages of submissions, so there is evidence of their hard work and dedication. Unless they're paid for their services, I will not be presenting my Defence case. How can they be remunerated for that? From the first day when I filed a request that my Defence case be refunded, I wanted to receive information about the costs of the Prosecution case against me. I never received that information. Then I sought information about how much of the UN funds is provided to finance all the cases of all other accused here and I was not given that information either. I was told that that information can be found on internet; however, I have no access to internet. Just like all other detainees at the Detention Unit, we are not entitled to internet access. Next, some ten years ago, the Registry drew up categories of the accused, first, second, and third. I was always assigned to the third category, and then once you made the decision that they need to start paying for my Defence case, they decided to review that, and I even sent a letter as to what category I should belong to. I guess they thought that they wanted -- that they thought that I wanted to be in the easiest category so that I could be relaxed while waiting for your Draconian judgement. I was been relaxed from day one because I am not interested in your judgement. I participate in these proceedings because I want to protect not only my own reputation and my honour but also many volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party and also in order to prove that all accusations against me are false, and I'm quite satisfied with the way things are going so far and have been going so far. Not all of the Trial Chambers seem to be alike. You have some major differences, but essentially all think alike. For the 18 months of preparation of the Defence case, other accused have received a sum of 380.000 euros. This is what indigent accused received. Eighteen months could turn into 24 months at the most. However, my pre-trial stage lasted for four years and eight months. This is why this amount needs to be doubled, that is to say 160.000 euros. For accused in third category, their defence costs 40.000 euros per month. Out of those 40.000 euros, 20.000 is allocated to lead counsel, and the rest to the other remaining members of the team. You can calculate how many months. So from the pre-trial phase, I'm entitled to 160.000 euros. You can deduct half for the fact that I represent myself, and then 380.000 euros need to be paid to the other members of my team. For every month of the trial, in November it will be four years, if you're going pay the monthly sum, that would come to 960.000 euros. Am I right? Yes, I'm right. I'm always right. So if you deduct half of that amount for the fact that I represent myself in the pre-trial stage and if we calculate only half of the amount for each month of the trial, that means that members of my team need to be paid about 1.300.000 euros. Unless that amount is paid, I will not be presenting my Defence case. I will not allow that members of my Defence team be humiliated in any way or as is popularly phrased here, that they be discriminated against. Since it is said that I like to discriminate against a lot of people, even English doctors, I do not like when my people are being discriminated against. It is believed that I oppose other forms of discrimination but endorse discrimination against my people. In addition to that, there are two other prerequisites that need to be met, and they are conditio sine qua non. I have been informed that in 2005, the OTP filed a motion for a contempt of court against me and that the Trial Chamber, and if I remember well, Mr. Antonetti, you were a member of that Chamber, and they denied that request. And later on, Judge Agius, or perhaps one of his legal officers, informed me that such a request had been filed and that it was denied. I insisted that this request or motion be provided to me and that I also receive the decision or the ruling denying that request. It is very important that I be provided this, and unless you provide this to me, I will not be presenting my Defence case. Recently, the OTP provided a number of binders with some documents, and then several days later they sent in their cavalry so that they could take those documents back from me. I was taken to the warden's office, and then they, escorted by the guards, went into my cell to requisition that material. There was an official of the Registry present there. She identified the documents. The documents were seized from the binders that were in my cell and then taken to the Registry and placed under seal there. I have to be given those documents again, and unless I receive them, I will not be presenting my Defence case. Your Honour, you remember that there have been a number of problems here concerning translation of Defence documents. I insisted that two of my most important books be translated into French and English, those are "Ideology of Serbian Nationalism" and "Roman Catholic Criminal Enterprise of the Artificial Croatian Nation." You first provided one deadline for that to be translated. You asked that that be translated into French, and then you asked me to find translators. I found a translation agency and then the Registry refused the services of that translation agency. Then they extended the deadline, and the last deadline that you set as the Trial Chamber was until the end of the Prosecution case. To this day I have not received the translation of those two books into English. I cannot draw up the concept of my defence without those two books, and was can see, most members of the Trial Chamber insist right now only on instigation, ignoring the other modes of perpetration, even though, in my opinion, that represents the violation of the spirit of Rule 98 bis, because they were supposed to give their opinion on all modes of commission and that if there is consensus, that at least some of the modes of commission be dropped. It would serve the judicial economy purposes. Since this has not been done, I have to defend myself against the entire indictment. The indictment remained intact including JCE commission, perpetration, aiding and abetting, instigation, and everything else. So without these two books, I cannot challenge the essence of the charges against me, which is hate speech, the so-called hate speech that all of you are prepared to accept as a crime even though there are no grounds for that in the international jurisprudence so far. You are invoking Streicher case, you are ignoring some other cases, but it will not be difficult for me to deal with all of you, especially since you have a tendency to invoke the jurisprudence of the ICTR while ignoring the fact that the crimes that that court is dealing with were committed one year after the indictment period in my case. All of the charges against me stop in 1993, whereas the genocide and persecutions in Rwanda were committed in 1994. Therefore, there's no use for you to invoke the jurisprudence of that Tribunal. However, it's your business what you're going to do. I have now just enumerated all of the obstacles for the Defence case. Unless you're prepared to remove all of these obstacles, then we'll simplify matters. Why don't you schedule the presentation of my opening arguments? I am entitled to four hours for that, and you cannot deny me that, whether there are witnesses, whether there is funding or anything else, you cannot deny me that. After presenting my opening speech, unless you meet all the requirements that I have just mentioned, we will move immediately to closing arguments unless you want this trial never to end, so that the residual mechanism has to deal with my case. And this is one of the funniest creations of the Security Council, this residual mechanism. It is even more ridiculous than the ad hoc tribunals. Unless these conditions of mine which are properly grounded in law are met -- they're also grounded on the Statute. The Statute guarantees that my Defence needs to be funded. In that case, I will need at least two years to prepare my Defence case. Why? Because the Prosecution needed four years and eight months. All right. Let us agree in advance that I'm more than twice smarter and capable than the entire Prosecution put together. Therefore, I don't need four years, but I need two years. In addition to that, I need 120 hours for examination-in-chief, which is what was accorded to the Prosecution without counting all of the abuse concerning additional tonnes of documents admitted into evidence without the presence of witnesses and without even reading the titles of those documents. I also intend to call 100 witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I didn't really understand. Could you make something clear, please. If by chance all these conditions you've mentioned are not met, you are asking us to directly go to the final judgement, closing arguments from the Prosecution and yourself? Is that what you want, or are you asking for two years to prepare for your -- to prepare your Defence case? I didn't understand this. I believe all of this is a bit contradictory. So could you make it clear, please. What exactly are you asking for if these conditions are not met? Do you want to directly go to the procedure for the final judgement, or do you want us to give you two years? Please make it clear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Lattanzi, the interpretation most likely was either incomplete or inaccurate. I said to you if you meet all of these conditions that are properly grounded in law, then I need the following, this is what I am seeking. Now, what you will approve out of that, two years, 100 witnesses and 120 hours, that is to be seen. So I stay within the provisions of the Statute. I ask these things and then you rule on them, and later on I can appeal if I'm not satisfied with this. However, these five matters that I mentioned earlier directly endanger my status here and my ability to present my Defence case. I have to know why six years ago the Prosecution wanted proceedings to be instituted against me. I am so curious I can't sleep. I have to know what were the documents that the UN cavalry seized from me six years ago. I have to know what those documents are. And also, the status of all of my legal advisors and case managers needs to be normalised. Two of them visited me recently, Nemanja Sarovic and others. They paid travel expenses for two legal advisors but not for two case managers. I have my Case Manager. My Case Manager is in charge of my legal advisors. So what am I to do? I will not allow anyone to humiliate me. And even though I may have humiliated Registry enough so far, I will not allow them to do the same to me. So these are my requirements without which I will not be presenting my Defence case. Unless you meet these requirements of mine which are completely justified, then I want you to set the date for my opening statement. I will not deny myself the pleasure of those four hours in the courtroom. You can do that even before the end of May. I'm prepared, just don't do it next week. Don't schedule it next week because my wife is coming to visit me and I will be caught in crossfire. So after the following week you can schedule a day for my opening statements and then after that we can proceed immediately to closing arguments. Unless I present my Defence case, I will not be filing my Defence final brief either, so that will additionally shorten the time. And if that suits you, then very well. Perhaps whether you will be able to convince the public that this was a fair trial is another matter. That's your problem. I know that the entire public will consider these requirements of mine to be fully justified and no lawyer can challenge what I have just told you and then it's up to you to see what you're going to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you have made a number of requests. The Trial Chamber will meet and deliberate on this. As of now, I cannot give you any answer. But there are simple things, however, where you can have clear indication right away. Obviously, you challenged this Chamber's decision on legal grounds. You're, of course, entitled to this, and you can appeal this decision made by the Trial Chamber. This is a right you're entitled to, and maybe the Appeals Chamber will disallow this Trial Chamber. Then --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you right away. I will not be filing an appeal, because you know that those Judges from the Appeals Chamber were always much worse than you. So there's no point in filing an appeal. I will be appealing the trial judgement, but as for your interlocutory decision, I will not be appealing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then a few years ago I was a Pre-Trial Judge for your case, which is absolutely right. I remember that the Chamber made a decision because by error the Prosecution had sent documents that you were not supposed to obtain. Now, I don't know how the Prosecution works. It's quite surprising, and the OTP wanted to get these documents back because you weren't supposed to have them, and the Pre-Trial Chamber had decided to retrieve them. It went with a representative of the OTP as well as a representative of the Registrar -- Registry to retrieve the documents, and now you're saying, Some documents were taken from me and I want them back. But I don't know what documents you're talking about. We'll look into this. Then you also said that there was a procedure for contempt of court. I have no recollection of this. It -- it seems that you're saying that there was -- there was no decision or a decision was handed down and it wasn't disclosed to you. I don't know. I'm going to look into this too, because I don't see why anything should be hidden from you. Now, regarding financing --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] I explain. The decision was made, but both the motion and the decision were ex parte, and I was informed in only one sentence that there had been a motion and that a decision was made rejecting the motion without ever explaining to me what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now we understand. It was an ex parte request made by the Prosecution and it was dismissed. You weren't told about it. So you are seizing this Trial Chamber with this issue. Very well, I will look into this with my fellow Judges. I really don't see why anything should be hidden from you now. Let's go back to finances. You know that the Trial Chamber has worked greatly in this direction. I undertook myself, against the will of my fellow Judges, to do things. I called upon my administration of your own country to know exactly what was your tax situation. The Serbian admin -- the administration of your country said it had disclosed all this information to the Registry. Then the Trial Chamber started a procedure. We rendered a decision. The Registrar was very unhappy with this decision and appealed, and then the Appeals Chamber in its majority with two dissenting Judges decided in our favour, which is why it was been decided you would be financed at 50 per cent, and now you're asking us for hundreds of thousands of euros. You gave us the exact number, the exact figure, but we'll deliberate among ourselves to see exactly what we will do. We'll take a look into this. But I must say that personally, I never tried to play hide and seek with you. I've always been fully transparent with you. This is what I believe. I believe, Mr. Seselj, that this problem of financing is not a problem, because intellectually you're far able to defend yourself, and you're the best person to know exactly the ins and outs of this case. You have a -- you're like an encyclopedia. You know everything about all this. On a transcript, you find that there's been a mistake in the translation. You can pick it right like that. So of course you can get help, but, you know, trust me, trust my experience, you're fully able to defend yourself, so it's not -- this question of financing is not a real problem. But it's true that legally you are entitled to it through the Statute. To tell you the truth, you know, when I was on Trial Chamber II, you filed a motion and I had started drafting an opinion saying that you were entitled to financing and that your associates could be paid back as long as they gave us the justification for your -- the receipts for your -- for the expenses incurred. And I still believe -- I still have the same opinion, but right when the opinion was about to be issued, the Trial Chamber changed and I could not voice my opinion. That's how things stand. This is how things were done. So I've always been very sensitive to this issue of financing, but I really believe, you know, that it's not a real problem for you, but we will render a decision. Since we've been seized of your request, we will render a decision. Because now the case is in your hands. You know that. Just like Judge Lattanzi said, she wanted to know exactly what you are intending to do. Are you going to present your case? Are you going to prepare your case? We need to know how long it is going to take, two years or what. If you want the trial to be expeditious, you can say, Ok, I will make a statement for four hours, the OTP does its closing arguments, I do my closing arguments. End of Story. We render the judgement. This is one possibility, just like also you could ask for extra time to prepare, which is what Mr. Karadzic is doing, for example, and then it's going to drag on for years. But, you know, you're saying you want a hundred witnesses, 120 hours. This gives rise to a series of problems. So, please, if I understood you correctly, as long as all the problems solved -- are not -- the problems you raised are not solved, you will not give us your 65 ter list; right? 65 ter (G)list.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because of those reasons. Not because that I'm clever. I'm fully aware of that. But that is not going to be the reason for me not to present my case. The reasons for not presenting my case would be those five that I have enumerated regulating the status of legal advisors, funding the Defence case, the document for contempt of court from 2005, the documents that had been seized in 2005, and the translation of those two books, "Ideology of Serbian Nationalism" and "Roman Catholic Project of Artificial Croatian Nation," in English, because that was the last position of the Registry. So those are my five conditions without which I will not be presenting my Defence case. And it's all based on law. My position is supported by the Statutes of the Tribunal, by general legal principles. I have to be aware of everything that concerns me, what documents had been seized from me and why. I don't care that the Prosecution made a mistake. I have to know what it was all about. Perhaps it could be of use to me. And I have to know why the Prosecution filed this motion for contempt of court and you rejected it. I have to know the reasons for that as well. Therefore, I will not be presenting my Defence case unless these Statutes -- issues of mine are resolved, because it makes my Defence case pointless. And regardless of how smart one is, one needs to have advisors outside. They need to go look for witnesses. They have to draw up witness statements. So there are a number of things that need to be done. They need to assist with proofing witnesses. Do you know how long it took the OTP to proof witnesses? They bring witnesses to The Hague a couple of days before their testimony and they make them learn by heart, like a poem to be recited, what they need to say during their testimony and then they check it. My witnesses will be reciting by heart everything they learn in advance they need to say. However, the Prosecution will not catch them lying as I was able to do with almost every Prosecution witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a small correction to make to the transcript. Yesterday, you said that there was -- that Milorad Vojnovic was a protected witness. I have the transcript here. Well, the day he testified, he testified without any protection measures. He was never granted any protective measures. So maybe there's been a mistake, but he has never been a protected witness. I have the transcript page to prove this. Mr. Marcussen, do you have anything to say? The interpreters worked wonderfully. They could even translate as fast as I was speaking, right in sync with myself, and I thank them from the very bottom of my heart. Thanks to them, we were able to finish on time, because they interpret extremely fast. So, Mr. Marcussen, please be extremely fast also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, one minute past time, I guess there isn't time for me to say much. Your Honours, the Prosecution may submit some material to you on some of the issues that the accused has raised, but the accused, it sounds to me, is essentially seeking that you reconsider a number of decision you have rendered; yet, he has not done anything to meet the standard for reconsideration. I would suggest that if the accused wants to pursue any of the claims he has made just now, he should file a written submission setting out the law that he is relying on so that becomes clear and we can respond to it. And as for the 65 ter (G) ruling that you rendered, he can seek certification to appeal that. I think he has said it's relevant to -- to challenge your order. He's basically just threatening that he's not going to put on a Defence case. It's up to him whether he wants to do it or not. Lastly, I just want to say that Rule 65 ter (G) also require the accused to disclose to the Prosecution his Defence exhibits. So we would also, from the Prosecution side, be expecting to receive the exhibits that he will be using. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. Your absolutely right. Very well. Mr. Seselj, do you want to speak again and then it will be done?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. President, I'm not threatening with anything. I'm just fighting for my rights and the five requirements that I made concern my fundamental rights. I'm not coming out with any threats. However, unless these five requirements of mine are not met, I will be mentioning them in the closing arguments. I will not be speaking about the merits of case. I will be addressing all of the violations of my rights since my arrival in The Hague. And in the Defence opening, I can tell you right away, that I will be mostly addressing this decision of yours and your dissenting -- partially dissenting opinion. This will be part of my opening. I will need about four hours, and I will be speaking a bit faster than you. I admire you for speaking that slowly. I could never speak slowly myself, just so you know. Once I'm done with four hours of Defence opening, unless you enable me to present my Defence case, you can schedule closing arguments right away, and I guess that the Prosecution's final brief is ready. I guess they've been working all of this time, and we will not need to wait for a long time for their final brief, or if we do need to wait for a long time, then this assumption that is being floated in the public very frequently will be confirmed, namely that The Hague Tribunal was tasked with keeping me here at any cost for as long as -- for -- until the -- another round of elections in Serbia is over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I can tell you that nobody told me to hold you here, to detain you here. I mean, I cannot speak on behalf of my fellow Judges, but nobody would dare to say such a thing to me. I'm a totally independent Judge, as you know. I know that there's going to be elections in your country soon. It's a cause for a major national debate, but I cannot factor that in. I mean, if you're here, you can -- you heard our decision to dismiss your motion for acquittal. Nobody told us to hold you here. You know that perfectly well, at least from me. Yes, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honour. I think the accused should maybe be advised he might be under the misapprehension that he can present an opening statement without presenting evidence. There would only obviously be a need for an opening statement if there is actually a Defence case. The opening statement is to lay out what the Defence evidence is going to be. So if the accused does not want to file 65 ter materials, then we move straight to closing briefings and closing arguments. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is simply not true. I am entitled to an opening statement. Nothing binds me to present any evidence. That's not an obligation I have. Maybe I have no evidence, but I am entitled to an opening statement. And look at another thing, Judges, if you have patience. I have, in theory, the right to make an opening statement of a defence and to inform you that I'm my own only witness and to submit myself to cross-examination. The Prosecution is making things up. It's nonsense. Nobody can challenge or deny me the right to an opening statement and in my opening statement, I will also be speaking about what kind of evidence I was about to present and why I was unable to, and that's what I will do to please the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've raised points of law and, of course, it is our duty to answer to them, but I want to thank everybody, interpreters first and foremost, but also the security officers, all the legal officers, ushers, and Registrar, and we shall reconvene as soon as possible. The hearing stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Rule 98 bis Judgement adjourned
